conviction_note: The findings net to zero: mild process positives (an on-time year-end report after two late ones, $10m of debt prepaid with the revolver undrawn, a public-safety operator as the preferred holders' board designee, Gilat saying the deal is 'progressing well') against mild negatives (a revenue run-rate of $106-107m for three quarters under a $109.3m consensus, no Allerium award announced since March after a 0.32x quarter, and the first print likely to present the sold S&S business as held for sale, which makes the headline non-comparable). p_up 45 rather than 50 comes from the name's own reaction function (1 of 7 prints up, median |18.1%|), which is a base rate and not a finding, times abs_move 16; the two measurements disagree in sign by a small margin and that gap is the reaction history, not the evidence.
bar: Revenue $109.3m and EPS -$0.35 from Earnings Whispers (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/CMTL, read 2026-10-14); other aggregators show $108.6m-$111.65m revenue and EPS -$0.28 to -$0.51 (Benzinga, Stocktwits via search). No company guide: the Q3 release states 'the Company has not provided future Non-GAAP financial guidance or targets' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000023197/000002319726000070/fy26q3ex991earningsrelease.htm, 2026-06-15). Two analysts: Northcoast Buy $2.50 initiated 2026-07-22, B. Riley Buy $6 dated 2025-10-06 (investing.com via search). The estimate sources disagree by about 3% on revenue and the bar is not company-guided, so every reported-quarter size here is capped small.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest 333.8K shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 1.6 days to cover, down from 565.6K on 2026-08-14 and 426.6K on 2026-09-15 (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/cmtl/short-interest/); 29,961,431 shares outstanding at 2026-06-11 (10-Q), so about 1.1% of shares out. Not crowded: no squeeze fuel on a good print and no squeeze cushion on a bad one. Options: chain unusable (ATM legs not two-sided, OI 1,103, put/call OI 0.3), so no skew statement exists. Holders: Magnetar and White Hat hold the $220.5m-liquidation-preference convertible preferred at a $7.99 conversion price with 9.99% blockers (White Hat 13D/A 2026-06-16); Vanguard Capital Management LLC filed a new 13G at 5.01% (1,503,083 shares) as of 2026-06-30 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/23197/000210011926001364/primary_doc.xml); Royce amended on 2026-07-28. Insider Form 4s since June are all RSU vesting with tax withholding (Gizinski 2026-08-11 at $1.73 and 2026-09-30 at $1.37); no open-market buys or sales. Tape: -14.8% over 20 sessions, -78.8% from the 52-week high, 7.6% above the low, $0.34m/day turnover.

findings.finding: Comtech will report fiscal Q4 and FY2026 on 2026-10-14 with no NT 10-K on file, against an NT 10-K on 2024-10-16 for FY2024 and an NT 10-K plus a 10-K filed in early November for FY2025; an on-time year-end close also delivers the audited FY2026 carve-out financial statements that are a buyer-side closing condition in the Gilat purchase agreement if closing falls after 2026-10-31.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The late FY2025 close was followed by the 2025-12-11 Q1 FY26 print, -15.5%; the FY2024 late-filing episode preceded the 2025-01-13 print, -43.3% (baseline). No print in the history has come on a clean, on-time year-end, so there is no observed reaction to this line.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock is 7.6% above its 52-week low and down 72% since the June print; if the market were paying for a cleaner reporting cycle the 20-day run-up would not be -14.8% into a scheduled, company-confirmed date. Prior NT 10-K at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/23197/000002319724000096/form12b-25_ntx10kx073124.htm (2024-10-16); the carve-out condition is in the 8-K at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/23197/000110465926073803/tm2617923d1_8k.htm (2026-06-15).
findings.independence: The company's own call notice fixes the date (https://comtech.com/press-releases/2026/10/09/comtech-to-host-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2026-earnings-conference-call/, 2026-10-09). The closing-condition link is the same June 8-K family as finding 3's warrant amendment background; counted once.

findings.finding: On 2026-07-31 Comtech made voluntary prepayments of $6.5m on the senior term loan and $3.5m on the subordinated priority term loan, on top of a $1.0m scheduled repayment, the lenders waived the FY2026 excess-cash-flow sweep, and the revolver was undrawn at the 2026-08-03 filing date; the $10.0m is Gilat's advance payment applied 65/35 under the credit agreements, so it is deal cash and not organic cash, but fiscal year-end liquidity was not under stress.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-06-15 print carried the credit amendments and the covenant suspension alongside the sale and fell 42.9%; the 2026-03-16 print (-24.5%) and 2025-12-11 (-15.5%) both carried liquidity commentary. This shareholder base has not paid for balance-sheet relief on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: Coverage is two analysts and the amendment drew no press; Northcoast's initiation (2026-07-22) predates it. The question lesson 4 asks is answered: the money bought debt reduction, not a ramp, so this is a zero-to-small positive rather than a growth signal.
findings.independence: Q3 10-Q: revolver balance of $3,641,000 repaid in May 2026 and total liquidity $49,389,000 at 2026-04-30 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/23197/000002319726000069/cmtl-20260430.htm, 2026-06-15).

findings.finding: The 2026-07-30 warrant amendment extends the lender warrant put right (up to 50% of 1,435,884 warrants at 90% of 30-day VWAP) to a newly defined 'Specified Permitted Individual Disposition' in the credit agreement, i.e. a specific further asset sale is contemplated by the lenders, consistent with the 2026-10-05 release's reference to 'further portfolio-shaping opportunities' and 'further financing initiatives'; a second divestiture announced with the print is a live possibility.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The one portfolio event in the history, the S&S sale on 2026-06-15, was bundled with a revenue miss and the stock fell 42.9%; no clean read exists.
findings.why_not_priced: The defined term is not reproduced in the filing and no analyst or article has discussed it; the market cap is $38m, so any disposition that reduces 16% subordinated debt (with a 50% make-whole before 2027-04-01) moves the equity stub either way. This is an inference from a defined term, sized as one.
findings.independence: Press release of 2026-10-05 language on 'further portfolio-shaping opportunities' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/23197/000002319726000088/exhibit991-pressreleasexco.htm). Proxy, not a company number.

findings.finding: Allerium's Q3 book-to-bill was 0.32x (after 1.06x and 2.51x in Q1 and Q2), which the company attributed to 'the timing of large, multi-year contract awards'; the company newsroom shows no Allerium award since the 2026-03-25 ACOG selection (only product launches on 06-18 and 06-23, a FirstNet board seat on 07-07 and a director appointment on 10-05), against a Q4 FY25 Allerium bookings comparable of $49.8m (0.81x), so the Q4 Allerium bookings line is at risk of a second weak quarter unless unannounced awards landed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The sweep says this name trades on bookings; the 2026-06-15 print with Allerium at 0.32x fell 42.9% (confounded by the sale and the revenue miss), and the 2025-11-10 print, the only up move (+7.0%), carried Q4 FY25 bookings of $94.4m.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market expected a bookings recovery the stock would not sit 7.6% off its low into the print; if it expected another 0.32x, the two analysts would have cut and Northcoast initiated at Buy on 2026-07-22. The absence of a press release is a proxy (not every award is announced) and S&S booked 1.04x in Q3, so consolidated bookings can clear even if Allerium is soft; sized net of that.
findings.independence: Q4 FY25 segment comparables from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/23197/000002319725000081/fy25q4ex991earningsrelease.htm (2025-11-10); the 0.32x and the 'timing' sentence from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000023197/000002319726000070/fy26q3ex991earningsrelease.htm (2026-06-15). The newsroom absence is a proxy.

findings.finding: Consolidated net sales have been flat at $106-107m for three quarters (Q1 FY26 guided $107-113m, Q2 $106.8m, Q3 $106.0m, the last a miss against $110.2m) while S&S is deliberately phasing out low-margin VSAT work; the Q4 revenue consensus of $109.3m sits about 3% above that run-rate with no company guide, so the base case is a small revenue miss of about 2%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 missed revenue by 4% with an EPS beat and fell 42.9% (bundled with the sale); Q2 FY26 fell 24.5%; Q1 FY26 fell 15.5%. Six of seven prints were negative; the name sells its prints.
findings.why_not_priced: A two-analyst consensus that has not been reset since the 2026-06-15 print is stale by construction; the aggregators disagree by about 3% ($108.6m-$111.65m) and there is no company guide, so this is capped small per the bar rule. Short interest at 1.1% means no squeeze cushion against a miss.
findings.independence: Q2 FY26 net sales $106.8m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/23197/000002319726000038/fy26q2ex991earningsrelease.htm, 2026-03-16); Q1 FY26 preliminary range $107-113m in the FY25 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/23197/000002319725000081/fy25q4ex991earningsrelease.htm, 2025-11-10). Shares a document with finding 4 (the Q3 release) for the Q3 revenue figure; different line.

findings.finding: The S&S business being sold was carried as 'held and used' at 2026-04-30 because the agreement was signed 2026-06-14; at the 2026-07-31 year-end the signed definitive agreement makes held-for-sale and discontinued-operations presentation likely, so the Q4 release may show continuing-operations revenue near the Allerium run-rate (~$56-61m) rather than the ~$109m consolidated figure the aggregators carry, producing mechanical 'miss' headlines while giving the retained business its first clean print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Comtech print has carried a discontinued-operations recast; the nearest analogue is the 2026-06-15 print where a presentation change (new segment names, pro forma retained-business metrics) accompanied a 42.9% fall.
findings.why_not_priced: Every estimate aggregator still carries a consolidated revenue number; none publishes a continuing-operations estimate, so the first recast lands on a bar built for the old perimeter. This is an accounting inference, not a company statement, and is sized as one.
findings.independence: The June 15 8-K's purchase agreement requires audited carve-out statements for FY2026 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/23197/000110465926073803/tm2617923d1_8k.htm), which implies the perimeter has been separated for audit; same filing family as finding 1's closing condition.

findings.finding: Gilat, the buyer, said on 2026-08-05 that 'the announced Comtech acquisition is progressing well' and is 'anticipated to close toward year-end', and its interim financials filed later still state closing 'by the end of 2026' subject to CFIUS, FTC and DOJ with no approval reported received; Comtech's own date is 'calendar Q4 2026', so tonight's call is the first scheduled chance for Comtech to report HSR expiry or CFIUS progress, or a slip into 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The deal announcement itself (2026-06-15) was sold, -42.9%, because the equity stub under $220m of preferred and ~$80m of post-sale debt is small; a confirmed on-time close would be the first positive deal datapoint.
findings.why_not_priced: A direct counterparty's statement that the process is on track, with Gilat funding from existing cash, has not moved CMTL (it fell from ~$1.73 in August to $1.27); the asymmetry is wide because a slip would push the make-whole and the Series B-4 exchange into 2027.
findings.independence: Gilat 6-K interim financials, Note 1c (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000897322/000117891326003967/exhibit_99-1.htm); Comtech's 'calendar Q4 2026' in https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000023197/000110465926073803/tm2617923d1_ex99-1.htm (2026-06-15).

findings.finding: Christopher D. Maloney, founder and former CEO of TriTech Software Systems (public-safety CAD/9-1-1, sold to Bain in 2018) and former CEO of SOMA Global, joined the board effective 2026-10-01 as Magnetar's designee under the 2026-06-14 Director Agreement, i.e. the preferred holders used their seat on a public-safety operator rather than a restructuring specialist.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock went from $1.37 (2026-09-30 tax-withholding price) to $1.27 after the 2026-10-05 announcement; the market read nothing into it.
findings.why_not_priced: A board appointment on a $38m-cap name with 1.1% short interest attracts no positioning; its value is as a read on the controlling preferred holders' intent, which no analyst has written about.
findings.independence: Form 3 for Maloney, no securities owned (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/23197/000215974626000003/wk-form3_1791584426.xml, 2026-10-09); the Director Agreement terms in the June 8-K (same document as finding 1's closing condition).

findings.finding: Jeff Robertson, President of Allerium, was appointed to the board of the First Responder Network Authority (FirstNet) by the Secretary of Commerce on 2026-07-07, a standing signal for the retained business's position in US public-safety procurement.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not a print line; no reaction observed.
findings.why_not_priced: Already public and ignored; filed because it bears on how the call frames Allerium's pipeline, which is the line the market trades.

findings.finding: Positioning is empty: short interest 333.8K shares (about 1.1% of 29.96m out), 1.6 days to cover and falling since mid-August; a new 5.01% holder (Vanguard Capital Management LLC, 1,503,083 shares as of 2026-06-30) filed after the June crash; insiders only vested RSUs. Neither side of the print has a squeeze mechanism.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prior prints moved 7-43% with short interest between 1% and 4.5% of float; positioning has not been the driver of this name's reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: Filed as context for the panel: it removes the squeeze argument from both sides and leaves the move to the fundamentals and the thin tape ($0.34m/day).

outside_window.finding: 625,000 lender warrants at $0.10 vest on 2026-10-17 unless the Closing Date Term Loans are repaid in full before then (they will not be, the sale is unclosed): about 2.1% dilution, known since June.

Closing of the $157.5m Gilat sale (expected calendar Q4 2026 / 'toward year-end'), with 65/35 debt paydown, the Series B-3 to B-4 exchange, voting agreements and the Allerium rename all triggered at close.

Subordinated make-whole steps from 50% to 75% of principal repaid after 2027-04-01, with 16% make-whole interest accruing from 2027-03-03; a closing that slips past March 2027 is materially more expensive.

searched_and_found_nothing: No pre-announcement, no NT 10-K and no 8-K other than the 2026-08-03 credit amendment and the 2026-10-05 director appointment in EDGAR submissions through 2026-10-14 (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0000023197.json).
No Nasdaq minimum-bid-price notice (no Item 3.01 8-K; the stock has stayed above $1).
No Allerium contract award on the company newsroom after 2026-03-25 (page 1 of comtech.com press releases read through 2026-10-09).
No HSR expiry or CFIUS clearance disclosed by either Comtech (8-Ks) or Gilat (Q2 release 2026-08-05 and interim 6-K financials).

No open-market insider purchase or sale since June: every Form 4 read (Gizinski 2026-08-11 and 2026-09-30) is RSU vesting with tax withholding; the 2026-10-01 Bondi and other filings carry the same 2026-09-30 period.

Q3 FY26 call transcript: gurufocus returned 403 and stocktaper 429, so management's Q4 commentary from the June call could not be read; the Q3 release itself contains no fourth-quarter or pipeline statements.
10-Q MD&A beyond character 100,000 was truncated by the fetcher; the Allerium bookings explanation was taken from the release instead.

The WebSearch budget was exhausted before a September 2026 news sweep and a peer NG9-1-1 award search (Intrado/Motorola/Carbyne) could be run; those two angles are unsearched, not empty.

baseline_tension: No skew exists (unusable chain); the 20-day run-up is -14.8% and the name is 7.6% off its low after six negative prints in seven, so the evidence set, which nets to zero, is slightly less negative than the tape and the reaction history, and p_up 45 sits between the two.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1: on-time report finding cut from +1.0 to +0.8 because this name has sold every process improvement so far (1 of 7 up).
Lesson 4: the debt prepayment was re-read as 'what did the money buy' (Gilat's advance applied to debt, not a ramp) and cut from +0.8 to +0.5.
Lesson 5: the 'Specified Permitted Individual Disposition' inference cut from +0.5 to +0.3 and the held-for-sale presentation inference kept at -0.5 but labelled as inference in the text.
Lessons 5 and 9: the Allerium no-award finding cut from -1.5 to -1.0 because the newsroom absence is a proxy and S&S booked 1.04x in Q3, so consolidated bookings can clear with Allerium soft.
Lesson 6: the revenue run-rate finding cut from -1.5 to -1.2 because the estimate sources disagree by ~3% and there is no company guide; `bar` says so and caps the reported-quarter sizes.
Lesson 7: short interest looked up (1.1%, 1.6 DTC) before the negatives were sized; not crowded, so no shrink on the negatives for squeeze risk.

Lesson 3: p_up left at 45 rather than pulled further from 50 because the only negative lean beyond the findings is the base rate, which the note names; the Maloney and FirstNet findings trimmed to +0.4 and +0.2.
Left standing: abs_move_pct 16 (lesson 8: thin tape and the name's own 18.1% median, not shrunk for uncertainty), the Gilat finding at +0.5 with its wide range, the positioning finding at 0.
